Now I'm tracing through the qtClustering algorithm carefully to make sure I preserve its exact semantics—iterating over unclustered seeds in ascending index order and greedily growing each candidate cluster.\n\nFor each candidate, I'm finding the next closest unclustered point by computing the max distance from it to all current members, accepting it only if that max distance is strictly below both the threshold and the current best diameter, with ties going to the lower index since it's encountered first. After generating candidates for every seed, the best cluster is chosen as the first one with strictly greater cardinality than the running best, again favoring lower seed indices on ties, and then it gets added while marking its members clustered. I note this is computationally expensive: for each outer iteration, every seed is reevaluated from scratch, so the complexity grows substantially with cluster size and point count—this is worth flagging as the main optimization target.\n\nI realize there's a real speedup available: since max distance over a set of members is exact regardless of the order it's computed in, I can maintain an incrementally updated max distance for each candidate as members are added, rather than recomputing the max over all members from scratch every time. Stats and final result printing only need to happen on root since the data is identical everywhere, though I'm now thinking about whether every rank should return the same exit code or just mirror whatever rank 0 computes during validation.\n\nFor validation itself, I'm leaning toward running the expensive check only on root and broadcasting the final valid/invalid flag to the rest, since duplicating this O(n²) work across every rank is wasteful. CMake's CUDA language detection with nvcc should work without extra fuss, so I'm moving on to check the results_output include path.\n\nI'm verifying that `hash` class and `distance` function names don't clash with anything, and that host-side validation code using these helpers compiles fine with std::min/max. I'm also double-checking the clustering time print statement and re-examining the original seed-skip logic in candidate cluster generation to make sure my grow kernel replicates it correctly.\n\nTracing through the growth loop termination conditions, I confirm my version matches the original: candidates with max distance exceeding the threshold are permanently ineligible since distances are non-decreasing, and among eligible candidates, the tie-breaking rule picks the lowest index when distances are equal, just like the original's strict less-than comparison. This gives identical selections (same ties to lowest index).\n- **Pruning (exact):** every member lies within the threshold of the seed, so `1 + #eligible neighbours` bounds a seed's cardinality. Seeds are visited in bound order and skipped once the bound is below the best found.\n- **CUDA:** one thread block grows one seed's cluster, with block-wide argmin and distance updates in shared memory.\n- **MPI:** seeds are split across ranks; each round the best (cardinality, lowest seed) is combined with `MPI_Allreduce`.\n- **OpenMP:** each rank runs worker threads, each driving a non-blocking stream on a local GPU and pulling chunks from a shared queue. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793091951369,"sessionID":"ses_e836af978ffeN2dqnmu1gnACqg","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01DEWeQjBSpmcd8XL84YtyJm","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/qtclustering_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp","content":"// QT Clustering Benchmark - Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA version\n//\n// QT (Quality Threshold) clustering is an algorithm that builds clusters\n// by starting with a seed point and iteratively adding the closest point\n// that maintains the cluster's diameter below a threshold. Every unclustered\n// point is tried as a seed each round; the largest candidate cluster (lowest\n// seed index on ties) is committed, and the process repeats until all points\n// are clustered.\n//\n// Parallelization:\n//  - CUDA:   one thread block grows the candidate cluster of one seed. Distance\n//            scans and the closest-candidate argmin are performed block-wide in\n//            shared memory.\n//  - OpenMP: each MPI rank runs one host worker thread per CUDA stream it owns\n//            (STREAMS_PER_DEVICE per local GPU). Workers pull seed chunks from a\n//            shared queue, so GPUs are kept busy regardless of seed cost.\n//            Cluster validation is also parallelized.\n//  - MPI:    the seeds of each round are distributed cyclically over ranks.\n//            Each round the best (cardinality, seed) pair is combined with\n//            MPI_Allreduce so every rank commits the identical cluster.\n//\n// Equivalence with the sequential algorithm:\n//  - A candidate's maximum distance to the cluster is maintained incrementally.\n//    Max over a set is order-independent, so this equals recomputing it.\n//  - A candidate whose maximum distance reaches the threshold can never become\n//    eligible again (the maximum only grows), so it is dropped permanently.\n//  - Selection is \"minimum max-distance, lowest point index on ties\", identical\n//    to the sequential scan order.\n//  - Seeds are pruned only when an upper bound on their cardinality (1 + number\n//    of eligible neighbours, since every member lies within the threshold of the\n//    seed) is strictly below a cardinality already achieved. Such seeds cannot\n//    win or tie, so the selected cluster is unchanged.\n//  - Floating-point contraction is disabled on host and device (-ffp-contract=off,\n//    --fmad=false) so CPU and GPU evaluate distances bit-identically.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <atomic>\n#include <cfloat>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdarg>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <numeric>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nstatic const double MAX_WIDTH = 20.0;\nstatic const double MAX_HEIGHT = 20.0;\n\n// Threads per seed-growth block. Must be a power of two.\nstatic constexpr int BLOCK_THREADS = 256;\n// Host worker threads (and CUDA streams) per local GPU.\nstatic constexpr int STREAMS_PER_DEVICE = 2;\n// Device scratch memory budget per worker for the growth workspaces.\nstatic constexpr size_t WORKSPACE_BUDGET = size_t(512) << 20;\n\n// Whether this process prints (rank 0 only).\nstatic bool g_root = true;\n\nstatic void rootPrintf(const char* fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));\nstatic void rootPrintf(const char* fmt, ...) {\n    if (!g_root) return;\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    vprintf(fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n}\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                        \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                              \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                              \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,    \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                  \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                       \\\n        }                                                                       \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Structure to represent a point in 2D space\nstruct Point {\n    double x, y;\n};\n\n// Structure to represent a cluster\nstruct Cluster {\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    int seed_point;\n};\n\n// Euclidean distance (same operation order on host and device)\n__host__ __device__ inline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    const double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    const double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\n// Generate synthetic 2D point data in clusters\nvoid generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n\n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n\n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n\n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n\n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n\n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Lexicographic candidate order: smaller max-distance first, then lower index.\n__device__ __forceinline__ bool candidateLess(double d1, int c1, double d2, int c2) {\n    return d1 < d2 || (d1 == d2 && c1 < c2);\n}\n\n// Upper bound per seed: number of unclustered points (other than the seed) within\n// the threshold. Every member of the seed's cluster lies within the threshold of\n// the seed, so cardinality <= 1 + outCount[i].\n__global__ void countCandidatesKernel(const int* __restrict__ seeds, int n,\n                                      const Point* __restrict__ pts,\n                                      const unsigned char* __restrict__ clustered,\n                                      int N, double threshold, int* __restrict__ outCount) {\n    const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i >= n) return;\n    const int seed = seeds[i];\n    const Point ps = pts[seed];\n    int cnt = 0;\n    for (int c = 0; c < N; ++c) {\n        if (c == seed || clustered[c]) continue;\n        if (distance(pts[c], ps) < threshold) ++cnt;\n    }\n    outCount[i] = cnt;\n}\n\n// Grow the candidate cluster of seeds[blockIdx.x]. One block per seed.\n//\n// Each step adds the eligible candidate with the smallest maximum distance to the\n// current members (ties: lowest index), exactly as the sequential greedy growth.\n// Candidates are kept in a compact active list (double-buffered in global memory)\n// with their running maximum distance to the members; candidates reaching the\n// threshold are removed permanently.\n//\n// outCard[blk] receives the cluster cardinality. If outMembers is non-null (used\n// for a single seed), the members are written in the order they were added.\n__global__ void growClusterKernel(const int* __restrict__ seeds, int n,\n                                  const Point* __restrict__ pts,\n                                  const unsigned char* __restrict__ clustered,\n                                  int N, double threshold,\n                                  int* __restrict__ wsIdx, double* __restrict__ wsDist,\n                                  int* __restrict__ outCard,\n                                  int* __restrict__ outMembers) {\n    __shared__ int cnt[2];\n    __shared__ int redI[BLOCK_THREADS];\n    __shared__ double redD[BLOCK_THREADS];\n\n    const int blk = blockIdx.x;\n    if (blk >= n) return;\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int seed = seeds[blk];\n    const Point ps = pts[seed];\n    const bool record = outMembers != nullptr;\n\n    int* const idxBase = wsIdx + size_t(blk) * 2 * N;\n    double* const distBase = wsDist + size_t(blk) * 2 * N;\n\n    if (tid == 0) {\n        cnt[0] = 0;\n        cnt[1] = 0;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    // Initial active list: unclustered points (other than the seed) within the threshold\n    for (int c = tid; c < N; c += BLOCK_THREADS) {\n        if (c == seed || clustered[c]) continue;\n        const double d = distance(pts[c], ps);\n        if (d < threshold) {\n            const int pos = atomicAdd(&cnt[0], 1);\n            idxBase[pos] = c;\n            distBase[pos] = d;\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    int cur = 0;\n    int card = 1;  // the seed\n    if (record && tid == 0) outMembers[0] = seed;\n\n    while (true) {\n        const int A = cnt[cur];  // uniform across the block\n        if (A == 0) break;\n\n        const int nxt = cur ^ 1;\n        const int* ci = idxBase + cur * N;\n        const double* cd = distBase + cur * N;\n        int* ni = idxBase + nxt * N;\n        double* nd = distBase + nxt * N;\n\n        // Block-wide argmin of (max distance, index)\n        double bd = INFINITY;\n        int bi = INT_MAX;\n        for (int k = tid; k < A; k += BLOCK_THREADS) {\n            const double d = cd[k];\n            const int c = ci[k];\n            if (candidateLess(d, c, bd, bi)) {\n                bd = d;\n                bi = c;\n            }\n        }\n        redD[tid] = bd;\n        redI[tid] = bi;\n        __syncthreads();\n        for (int s = BLOCK_THREADS / 2; s > 0; s >>= 1) {\n            if (tid < s && candidateLess(redD[tid + s], redI[tid + s], redD[tid], redI[tid])) {\n                redD[tid] = redD[tid + s];\n                redI[tid] = redI[tid + s];\n            }\n            __syncthreads();\n        }\n        const int chosen = redI[0];\n        const Point pc = pts[chosen];\n\n        // Update running maxima with the new member and keep eligible candidates\n        for (int k = tid; k < A; k += BLOCK_THREADS) {\n            const int c = ci[k];\n            if (c == chosen) continue;\n            const double m = fmax(cd[k], distance(pts[c], pc));\n            if (m < threshold) {\n                const int pos = atomicAdd(&cnt[nxt], 1);\n                ni[pos] = c;\n                nd[pos] = m;\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (tid == 0) {\n            if (record) outMembers[card] = chosen;\n            cnt[cur] = 0;  // consumed buffer becomes the next output buffer\n        }\n        ++card;\n        cur = nxt;\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (tid == 0) {\n        outCard[blk] = card;\n    }\n}\n\n// Pack (cardinality, seed) so that a larger key is a larger cardinality, and on\n// equal cardinality a smaller seed index. Key 0 means \"no candidate\".\nstatic uint64_t encodeCandidate(int card, int seed) {\n    return (uint64_t(card) << 32) | uint64_t(0xFFFFFFFFu - uint32_t(seed));\n}\n\nstatic void decodeCandidate(uint64_t key, int& card, int& seed) {\n    card = static_cast<int>(key >> 32);\n    seed = static_cast<int>(0xFFFFFFFFu - static_cast<uint32_t>(key & 0xFFFFFFFFull));\n}\n\n// Per-device execution context. Each worker owns one non-blocking stream and its\n// own device buffers, so several workers can share a device concurrently.\nstruct GpuWorker {\n    int device = -1;\n    int chunkCap = 0; nullptr;               // N seed ids\n    int* out = nullptr;                 // N cardinalities / upper bounds\n    int* ws_idx = nullptr;              // chunkCap * 2N\n    double* ws_dist = nullptr;          // chunkCap * 2N\n    int* members = nullptr;             // N (single-seed record)\n};\n\nstatic GpuWorker makeWorker(int device, const std::vector<Point>& points) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    GpuWorker g;\n    g.device = device;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(device));\n\n    int sms = 1;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, device));\n\n    const size_t bytesPerBlock = size_t(2) * N * (sizeof(int) + sizeof(double));\n    const size_t budgetBlocks = std::max<size_t>(1, WORKSPACE_BUDGET / bytesPerBlock);\n    const size_t wanted = std::max<size_t>(64, size_t(sms) * 4);\n    g.chunkCap = static_cast<int>(std::min({wanted, budgetBlocks, size_t(N)}));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&g.stream, cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.pts, size_t(N) * sizeof(Point)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.clustered, size_t(N)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.seeds, size_t(N) * sizeof(int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.out, size_t(N) * sizeof(int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.members, size_t(N) * sizeof(int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.ws_idx, size_t(g.chunkCap) * 2 * N * sizeof(int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&g.ws_dist, size_t(g.chunkCap) * 2 * N * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(g.pts, points.data(), size_t(N) * sizeof(Point),\n                          cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    return g;\n}\n\nstatic void freeWorker(GpuWorker& g) {\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(g.device));\n    cudaFree(g.pts);\n    cudaFree(g.clustered);\n    cudaFree(g.seeds);\n    cudaFree(g.out);\n    cudaFree(g.members);\n    cudaFree(g.ws_idx);\n    cudaFree(g.ws_dist);\n    cudaStreamDestroy(g.stream);\n}\n\n// Main QT clustering algorithm (hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA)\nstatic std::vector<Cluster> qtClustering(const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                         const double threshold,\n                                         std::vector<GpuWorker>& workers,\n                                         const int rank, const int nranks) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    const int W = static_cast<int>(workers.size());\n    GpuWorker& primary = workers[0];\n\n    std::vector<unsigned char> clustered(N, 0);\n    std::vector<int> unclustered(N);\n    std::iota(unclustered.begin(), unclustered.end(), 0);\n    std::vector<Cluster> clusters;\n\n    std::vector<int> mySeeds;\n    std::vector<int> sortedSeed;\n    std::vector<int> sortedUB;\n\n    while (!unclustered.empty()) {\n        // Current clustered mask on every device\n        for (GpuWorker& g : workers) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(g.device));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(g.clustered, clustered.data(), size_t(N),\n                                       cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, g.stream));\n        }\n\n        // Seeds owned by this rank (cyclic over the unclustered list, which is the\n        // same on every rank)\n        mySeeds.clear();\n        for (size_t i = size_t(rank); i < unclustered.size(); i += size_t(nranks)) {\n            mySeeds.push_back(unclustered[i]);\n        }\n        const int nMine = static_cast<int>(mySeeds.size());\n\n        // Cardinality upper bounds for this rank's seeds\n        std::vector<int> ub(nMine, 1);\n        if (nMine > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(primary.device));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(primary.seeds, mySeeds.data(), size_t(nMine) * sizeof(int),\n                                       cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, primary.stream));\n            const int threads = 128;\n            countCandidatesKernel<<<(nMine + threads - 1) / threads, threads, 0, primary.stream>>>(\n                primary.seeds, nMine, primary.pts, primary.clustered, N, threshold, primary.out);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(ub.data(), primary.out, size_t(nMine) * sizeof(int),\n                                       cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, primary.stream));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(primary.stream));\n            for (int& u : ub) u += 1;  // count of neighbours + the seed itself\n        }\n\n        // Visit seeds by decreasing bound so good clusters are found early and the\n        // remaining seeds can be pruned.\n        std::vector<int> order(nMine);\n        std::iota(order.begin(), order.end(), 0);\n        std::sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [&](int a, int b) {\n            return ub[a] != ub[b] ? ub[a] > ub[b] : mySeeds[a] < mySeeds[b];\n        });\n        sortedSeed.resize(nMine);\n        sortedUB.resize(nMine);\n        for (int k = 0; k < nMine; ++k) {\n            sortedSeed[k] = mySeeds[order[k]];\n            sortedUB[k] = I suspect the bottleneck is in chunk serialization—once pruning kicks in after the first chunk, most seeds get eliminated, so the work ends up dominated by that initial pass.\n\nI want to double-check hash consistency across different rank counts for N=5000 with the -r flag, and verify N=20000 behaves similarly, though that can wait for the perf log run later. I'm also reviewing correctness concerns: the upper-bound pruning loop against sorted descending bounds looks right, the global-best load across ranks needs to be race-safe, each omp worker thread uses its own stream per device, the count pass sizing against mySeeds and N looks fine, and I'm checking memory budget math for chunk capacity times working-set size at N=20000.\n\nNow I'm verifying the growClusterKernel bounds check against chunkCap, confirming shared memory sizing for redI, checking that outMembers writes stay within card < N, and confirming the rootPrintf format-attribute declaration/definition pairing is fine. I also want to rebuild cleanly and inspect the full compiler output for any -Wextra or nvcc warnings that might have been filtered out, and double check that CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES covers sm_89/sm_90 properly with the installed nvcc and cmake minimum version.\n\nI'm also tracing through the OpenMP parallel region: confirming the workers vector references are taken after all push_backs complete, checking MPI_Allreduce behaves correctly when some ranks have zero unclustered items, and verifying CUDA_CHECK failures inside the parallel region correctly trigger MPI_Abort without deadlocking. I should test edge cases like \"-h\", invalid args, zero/negative parameters, and device-sharing scenarios (ranks > GPUs, GPUs > ranks) to confirm behavior matches the original implementation.\n\n","time":{"start":1793092943494,"end":1793092953882},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"text","timestamp":1793093160892,"sessionID":"ses_e836af978ffeN2dqnmu1gnACqg","part":{"id":"prt_17cae4055001rPv7TjmhZ3MrxE","messageID":"msg_17cae3c0d001L9Gjug1QeZ26oF","sessionID":"ses_e836af978ffeN2dqnmu1gnACqg","type":"text","text":"I rewrote `qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp` as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program and updated `qtclustering/CMakeLists.txt`. The executable name is still `qtclustering`, and no files were added. Output matches the original on every case I compared (N from 31 to 2000, several thresholds, 1 to 4 ranks), and runs are far faster: N=1000 went from 7.0 s to about 0.2 s, and N=5000, which took over 2 minutes, runs in about 0.5 s.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- **Algorithm (exact):** the original recomputes every candidate's maximum distance to all members on each step. The port maintains that maximum incrementally, drops candidates that reach the threshold for good, and keeps the same tie-breaking (lowest index). Seeds are also skipped when an upper bound on their cluster size is below a size already found, so they cannot change the result.\n- **CUDA:** one thread block grows one seed's cluster, with block-wide argmin and distance updates in shared memory.\n- **OpenMP:** each rank runs worker threads, each driving a stream on a local GPU and pulling seed chunks from a shared queue. Cluster validation is parallelised too.\n- **MPI:** seeds are split across ranks each round, and the best (cardinality, seed) pair is combined with `MPI_Allreduce`.\n- **Numerics:** FMA contraction is disabled on both host and device so CPU and GPU distances are bit-identical. I checked that this doesn't change the original's output.\n- **CMake:** the single `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA source so the kernels stay in the existing file. It links MPI, OpenMP and CUDA with no new dependencies. The default architectures are sm_80 through sm_90, and this 3090 box is sm_86.\n\n**Behaviour to know about**\n\n- CUDA is unconditional, as requested. The program aborts if no GPU is visible; there is no CPU fallback.\n- Ranks on a node split the node's GPUs. If there are more ranks than GPUs, ranks share them.\n- Scaling across ranks is modest at these sizes. N=20000 went from about 3.2 s on one rank to 2.5 s on four.\n- I did not change the original generator, which loops forever for N ≤ 30 (`group_cnt` is always 0), so the new program hangs there too. Fixing it would change behaviour for those inputs, so I left it and can address it if you want.\n\nI tested with Open MPI 4.1.6 on four RTX 3090s, using ranks from 1 to 8 with and without GPU sharing. The build is warning-free. I built in a scratch directory outside the workspace so no build artifacts were added there.","time":{"start":1793093156949,"end":1793093160888}}}
